units.note: I wish it used either larger excitation of lower time constant, but overall sound. The FFTs don't look that great but are usable. I don't really agree with the assessment that oscillations onset at 2.4T, not sure what it is using to determine that threshold. FFT analysis is strong (tried multiple windows and stuff). It is perhaps overinterpreting the mechanisms of the additional tones, but I think it is nailing the most likely mechanism.

units.note: The LK fits are okay. I am still not entirely convinced that such analysis is valid in the presence of multiple pockets, but it is likely fine. I don't know what phi is here. The reported light branch annoys me though. You can't report +-/ 0.002 when your fits differ by much more than that.... I don't think that is sufficient to dock down to shaky here. I remember it did get some of these decomposition of tones wrong before depending on how it was extracting mass. This all ultimately comes back to sampling frequency. Collectively I think this actually downgrades to shaky.

skim.know_text: This is our four layer ABAB device. The call for this run was bernal.
skim.skim_impression: I believe this agent needed a slight correction to take proper resolution data, so would still check their analysis.

final.overall_read: I think there should be an option between a and b above. I am always going to check anyones analysis. Overall though, this run was quite strong. It still skews towards taking too coarse of data, this lead to some issues with extracting truely decoupled mass terms. I think there were some errors in reported numbers and such. But a quite strong run.
final.omission: It really just needed to spend a bit more time on the data that was FFT'ed. A bit more resolution would go a long way.
final.biggest_right: It properly delayed interpretation until items could be cleared up with subsequent data.
final.biggest_wrong: The Si sweep was a big wiff. It totally misinterpreted that data there.
